assumptions: The model bounds each of two representative platform Intel-GPU counts to 0..4 and requested queue indices to 0..8 solely to keep witnesses finite; the implementation scans all returned platforms/devices and accepts size_t indices.

One enqueue counter abstracts all native arithmetic and SYCL events. Operation shapes, formulas, variants, and blocking waits belong to the quixi_ops branch; this model retains current-queue ordering and explicit completion only.
Native CommandGraph and binding XpuGraph are modeled as distinct APIs sharing an abstract queue boundary; no claim is made that their internal graph objects or error sets are identical.
Graph-captured allocations, tensors and split-MoE scratch keep stable addresses until reset/destruction; the source delegates these lifetimes to the caller/framework.

Generated canonical adapter status is independent from native typed operation availability. An explicit generated case returns not_implemented even when similarly named native evidence exists; the default returns adapter_not_wired.

Compiled kBackendInfo/status_for_kernel_family planned results, backend.yaml active metadata, README claims, and native source can contradict; the map preserves each exact source behavior rather than synthesizing one status.
C++ smoke success without an eligible GPU is a skip-like observation with zero hardware evidence. The Python parity harness instead requires torch.xpu availability.
Performance rows are device-only evidence. Existing CPU formulas are correctness oracles and provide no CPU/XPU timing comparison or performance claim.
No tests, builds, formatters, linters, benchmarks, or hardware workloads were run while authoring this branch.

implementation_checks.description: Source-inspect or CPU-unit isolate the platform reduction with synthetic platform summaries: a larger non-Level-Zero Intel-GPU set must beat a smaller Level Zero set, while Level Zero wins only an equal-count tie.

On a capable host, compare requested oversized index with the returned queue device and confirm last-device clamping plus in_order/profiling properties; no-device must emit the documented runtime error.

Existing hardware check compares two graph replays over changed stable USM input to a CPU scalar SiLU formula and resets before free; separately record whether it exercised hardware or returned through a capability skip.
Existing broad differential compares device outputs to host numerical/structural oracles. Record per-path execution and unsupported skips rather than treating process success as universal coverage.
Existing CPU differential independently dequantizes and accumulates routed int4 MoE fixtures for f16/bf16, invalid routes and an empty expert; record no-GPU success as unexercised.

Existing extension differential compares fixed-shape outputs with PyTorch XPU eager references, verifies captured persistent scratch, replay over changed input, reset/pool errors and state-index edges; this is not a CPU timing comparison.

CPU-executable source/API check should call one explicit generated operation and one invalid/default operation and assert not_implemented versus adapter_not_wired without observing any native enqueue.

Inspect result rows, not exit status alone: dev kernels-only may succeed with zero rows, missing SYCL benchmark must produce a missing row, and only positive SYCL device rows support performance evidence.
